CausalChain: Androgen receptor activation -> upregulation of HK2 expression -> enhanced aerobic glycolysis (increased glucose uptake, ATP production, and lactate secretion) -> establishment of an acidic microenvironment and promotion of immune evasion and sorafenib resistance -> inhibition of AR and HK2 -> reduction in glycolytic flux and acidification -> increased apoptosis and restored sensitivity to sorafenib.
Hypothesis: In HCC, AR signaling upregulates HK2-mediated aerobic glycolysis, which contributes to sorafenib resistance; therefore, combined inhibition of AR and HK2 will disrupt this metabolic reprogramming, decreasing tumor growth and overcoming drug resistance.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a formidable clinical challenge due largely to metabolic reprogramming and the consequent drug resistance seen with treatments such as sorafenib. Although a wealth of evidence implicates enhanced aerobic glycolysis in tumor proliferation, immune evasion, and metastasis, emerging data suggest that sex hormone signaling—particularly through androgen receptors (AR)—may critically reinforce this metabolic phenotype. Here, we propose that AR-driven upregulation of glycolytic enzymes, with hexokinase 2 (HK2) as a key mediator, establishes a feed-forward mechanism that not only sustains the Warburg effect but also contributes to sorafenib resistance. Accordingly, we hypothesize that dual inhibition of AR signaling and HK2 may synergistically disrupt glycolytic flux, impair HCC progression, and restore drug sensitivity. This work outlines a potential therapeutic strategy targeting both hormonal and metabolic pathways, which is especially pertinent given the male predominance in HCC incidence.
